title: Three stored-entry deletions can reverse a selected WT-to-unc31 worm gain cycle when retained means stay positive
abstract: We tested a published cross-strain cell-gain constraint by deleting stored response entries. Its six-edge cycle uses 12 WT and unc31 lists with 137 entries. All list means match stored means, but nine lengths differ from occurrence counts. Exact subset search and budget allocation show that no one- or two-entry deletion can reverse the cycle sum while retained means stay positive. Three entries from one WT list move the sum from -2.583612 to +0.207330. Two deletions can make a mean nonpositive, so the result is conditional. Global enumeration of 137 single and 9316 double removals confirms the bounds. This is a sensitivity test of pooled entries, not a confidence interval, exact gain fit, cleaning rule or biological strain effect. Animal and event IDs are absent. Original code, aggregates, hashes, a figure and external regeneration steps support reproduction.

display.caption: Exact cycle-sum extrema with up to three deletions and positive retained means. Two deletions can make a mean nonpositive outside this scope.

citations.reason: Tests deletion sensitivity of its cross-strain cycle. The original bound is not a new claim.
Extends entry-deletion analysis from a different within-WT reciprocity cycle. All code is new.
